property_summary: Deposits with value exactly equal to MinDeposit are always ignored by the reference, so the balances map never changes for such deposits; the buggy version accepts them and increases the sender's balance, breaking the invariant that msg.value == MinDeposit implies no balance change.

A Deposit that makes the sender's balance overflow (via msg.value extremely large) leaves balances[sender] correct in P (revert due to require) but corrupt in M (wraps around), so for all inputs P's balances are always >= previous balance after a non-reverting Deposit, while M fails this for some input.

After a successful Deposit, the caller's balance plus all other balances never exceeds the total supply of the token, but the buggy version allows overflow of individual balances, making the sum of all balances inconsistent with the deposited amounts.

After any non-reverting Deposit through C, reading the caller's balance via the public getter must return a value at least as large as msg.value, but the buggy version wraps on overflow causing the balance to be smaller.

For any sequence of calls, the sum of all balances in C must be at least the total Ether received by the contract (excluding direct transfers), but the mutant allows an individual balance to overflow, causing the total tracked balances to under-represent the actual deposits.

After any sequence of Deposit calls, the sum of all individual deposits made by an address must equal its balance, but the mutant sets the balance to the last deposit amount instead of accumulating, so a second deposit for the same address breaks this invariant.

For any two calls to Deposit by the same sender (with different values above MinDeposit in either order), the final balance of that sender must equal the sum of the two deposit amounts; the mutant sets balance to the second deposit amount instead of accumulating.
After a sender performs a Deposit above MinDeposit, the sender's balance must increase by msg.value; the mutant sets the balance to msg.value instead of adding msg.value.

After a Deposit above MinDeposit by a sender who already had a positive balance, the sender's balance must strictly exceed the deposit amount; the mutant sets the balance to the deposit amount, erasing the prior balance.
After two consecutive deposits by the same sender, the balance of the sender in the reference equals the initial balance plus both deposits, while the mutant sets it to only the last deposit amount.

In the reference contract, a deposit with msg.value > MinDeposit that would cause an overflow in the receiver's balance reverts (via the require check), so balances remain unchanged; in the buggy contract the balance is incremented before the check, so an overflow-causing deposit reverts but the balance has already been wrongly increased, leaving a different balance.
For any address, after a Deposit that reverts due to overflow, the balance of that address in the reference contract remains unchanged from before the call, while in the mutant it may increase.
If Deposit() reverts, balances must remain unchanged for the caller; the mutant increments the caller's balance before the require check, so a reverting deposit can still increase balances.

After any call to Deposit() that reverts due to overflow, the caller's balance must remain unchanged; the mutant increments balances before the require check, causing a persistent increase for a failing deposit.

For any address, after any Deposit that reverts, the balance of any other address must match its balance at the time of the last successful deposit seen by that address; the mutant can increment the caller's balance before the require check, so a reverting overflow deposit can leave the caller's balance higher than the last successful deposit for that caller while keeping other balances unchanged, violating the invariant that balances only change on successful deposits.

After any deposit, the reference C only updates balance and logs when msg.value > MinDeposit, while the mutant updates and logs for any msg.value, so balances and History length can diverge for deposits <= MinDeposit.
After any Deposit call, the sender's balance must be at least the amount sent; the mutant subtracts msg.value instead of adding it, violating this invariant.
After a successful Deposit, the sender's balance should equal the previous balance plus the deposit amount, but the mutant subtracts instead.
After a Deposit, the contract's recorded balance of the sender increases by at least msg.value (or the call reverts); the mutant decreases it instead.

After a successful Deposit, the sender's balance recorded in c.balances must be strictly greater than before the call; the mutant subtracts msg.value, causing it to fail this strictly-increasing invariant for any deposit above MinDeposit.

For any valid deposit above MinDeposit, the sum of all recorded balances equal to the total ether received by the contract, which the mutant breaks by subtracting msg.value from balances instead of adding it.

After any successful deposit, reference C emits a History update via TransferLog, while the mutant does not; thus reading TransferLog's History length must strictly increase after a qualifying deposit on reference but not on mutant.

After a deposit with msg.value > MinDeposit, the contract's balance must increase by msg.value; the reference satisfies this for all inputs, but the mutant (which skip-logs) still satisfies this rule, so this difference cannot be detected via balance changes; we must detect the log itself: the TransferLog's History length must increase by exactly 1 after a successful deposit in the reference, but the mutant never calls AddMessage, so the length stays unchanged, making the mutant violate this invariant.

After a successful deposit (msg.value > MinDeposit), the History length of the TransferLog must be strictly greater than its length before the call; the mutant omits the AddMessage call so the length remains unchanged.
After a successful deposit where msg.value > MinDeposit, the TransferLog's History array length must increase by exactly 1; the mutant skips the Deposit logging call, so its length remains unchanged.
After a Deposit with msg.value > MinDeposit, the TransferLog History length must increase by exactly 1; the mutant omits the AddMessage call so the length remains unchanged.
A user should be able to withdraw exactly their entire balance; the mutant prevents this by requiring strict inequality, so it reverts when _am equals the full balance.

A user must be able to CashOut an amount exactly equal to their full balance, leaving a balance of zero; the mutant reverts for this specific case because it requires _am < balance instead of _am <= balance.

For any admissible input where msg.sender has a balance, a CashOut of exactly that full balance must succeed and reduce the balance to zero; the mutant reverts because it treats _am == balances[msg.sender] as disallowed.

For any address with a positive balance, a CashOut of exactly that balance must succeed and leave the balance at zero; the mutant incorrectly reverts because its strict '<' check excludes the equality case.

For any caller whose balance 'b' is at least MinDeposit+1 (ensuring a deposit occurred) and any amount 'am' in (0, b], CashOut(am) must not revert; the buggy version reverts when am == b because it uses strict less-than instead of less-than-or-equal.

For any account and any amount ≤ its balance, calling CashOut(amount) must reduce the caller's balance by exactly that amount; the mutant skips the balance decrement, leaving the balance unchanged while still sending ether, so the post-condition 'balance decreased by amount' fails.

For any initial balance and any withdrawal amount not exceeding the balance, the caller's balance after CashOut must equal the initial balance minus the amount; the mutant fails to decrement the balance, so the post-condition balance == initial - amount is violated.

For any non-zero withdrawal amount not exceeding caller's balance, CashOut must decrease caller's balance by exactly that amount; the mutant skips balance deduction, so balance remains unchanged while still sending ether.

After CashOut is called with any _am ≤ caller's balance, the sum of caller's balance and history message value must equal the sum before the call; the mutant skips balance decrement, so balance+lastMsg.Val is too large.
After a CashOut call, the caller's balance must decrease by at least the amount specified; the mutant skips balance deduction, leaving the balance unchanged while still transferring ether.

In the reference contract, a CashOut call for amount exceeding the caller's balance always reverts due to the underflow of the subtraction; in the mutant, where the condition is replaced by true, it does not revert and allows an overdraw.
After a Deposit followed by a CashOut, the caller's balance must never fall below zero; the mutant enables overdraw, making the balance underflow to a huge value instead of reverting.
For any address with no ETH in the contract, calling CashOut with any non-zero amount must revert; the mutant allows the call to proceed and reduces the caller's balance (causing underflow).
For any caller whose balance is less than the requested amount, CashOut must revert; the mutant always allows the call, causing an underflow.
Calling CashOut with an amount exceeding the caller's balance must revert in the reference but succeeds in the mutant, causing a state divergence observed via the caller's balance or revert status.

After any CashOut, the caller's actual ETH balance increase equals the amount deducted from their internal balance in the reference contract, but the bug sends 0 ETH, so the rule fails for any positive amount.
After a deposit and a CashOut, the receiver's ETH balance must increase exactly by the amount deducted from C's internal balances, but the bug sends 0 wei.
After a successful CashOut, the contract's ETH balance must decrease by the requested amount, but the bug sends 0 wei so the contract's ETH balance decreases less than the amount.
After a successful CashOut, the contract's ETH balance must not exceed its prior balance minus the amount, but the bug sends 0 wei, so the contract retains more ETH than allowed.
After a CashOut that does not revert and deducts an internal balance, the recipient received exactly the requested amount of Ether, but the mutant sends 0 wei.

A user's balance must always correspond to the net Ether deposited minus successfully withdrawn, ensuring no underflow or balance-invariant violation; the bug allows withdrawing more than deposited, breaking this invariant.
After a CashOut, the sum of all balances in c never exceeds the contract's Ether balance; the mutant allows underflow that creates a balance larger than available Ether.
For any call to CashOut, the caller's balance after the call is never less than before minus the requested amount; the buggy version allows underflow, making the balance much larger instead.

After any Deposit and CashOut sequence where every cashout amount is at most the caller's balance, the contract balance and sum of all balances are equal; the mutant breaks this because underflow allows withdrawing more than deposited, creating extra balance tokens without corresponding Ether.
After any call to CashOut by a caller with a positive balance, the caller's balance strictly decreases; the mutant can increase the balance due to underflow when _am exceeds the current balance.

After a CashOut, the caller's balance plus the original contract's Ether balance must remain equal to the sum of all deposits (invariant broken by the mutant because the caller's balance increases while Ether is still sent out).
After a successful CashOut, the caller's balance must decrease by at least the requested amount; the bug increases it instead, violating the condition.
After a successful CashOut, the caller's balance must decrease by exactly the requested amount; the bug increases it instead.
